clue.text: 31 club

definitions.meaning: the answer at 31 across is a word for a flavouring, and this is one such seasoning made from nutmeg husks
a heavy spiked staff once carried as a weapon

explanation.walkthrough: '31' points to the solution at 31 across, so read it as a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: a spice ground from the outer husk of nutmeg, and a medieval spiked war club.

clue.text: 31 for king, perhaps, taking a little time to mature, initially

parts.note: a king is one example of a playing card
MO is short for moment, a little time

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of the word mature

explanation.surface: Someone waits for a royal figure to ripen slowly over time.
explanation.walkthrough: '31' means the solution at 31 across, so the definition is a spice; 'taking' just links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic pod is an example of a culinary spice, used widely in Indian cooking.

clue.text: My editor's a stud!

definitions.meaning: the editor is the person in charge of me, my chief
a stud is a raised ornamental knob, as on a shield

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that their editor is a handsome womaniser.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a manager or chief; the other is a raised knob or ornament, like the centre of a shield.

clue.text: Stretcher made of sandalwood?

parts.note: read 'sandalwood' as a piece of wood for a sandal: a footwear form that keeps leather stretched, not a hospital stretcher of fragrant timber

explanation.definitionFit: This wooden or plastic form is inserted into footwear to keep it stretched and in shape.

clue.text: 31 girl with fan on top

indicators.note: in a down clue, on top places the fan piece above the girl

parts.note: a fan or enthusiast is a nut, as in a fitness nut
Meg is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman has an admirer perched above her.
explanation.walkthrough: '31' means the solution at 31 across, a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: This seed of a tropical tree is an example of a spice, grated into puddings and drinks.

clue.text: Unfashionable Duke caught by aristocrat, given reprimand

indicators.note: caught by puts the shortened name inside the aristocrat word

parts.note: a toff is slang for an upper-class person

indicators.note: ton is an old word for fashion, so the unfashionable version of the name loses those letters

parts.note: Duke Ellington was the American jazz bandleader

explanation.surface: A nobleman scolds an out-of-date duke he has collared.
explanation.walkthrough: Duke Ellington was the jazz bandleader. 'Unfashionable' uses the old word ton, meaning fashion, as in 'bon ton'; 'caught by' is the container signal and 'given' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A scolding or rebuke, as when a child is told sternly that they behaved badly.

clue.text: 31 girl …

definitions.meaning: points to the solution at 31 across, so a spice is wanted, here a pungent root
a nickname for a red-haired girl

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on into 8 down, where this light pairs with a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: The knobbly root used as a hot spice, and also a nickname or name for a girl.

clue.text: possibly with it to wear the crown?

parts.note: to wear the crown is to be the monarch, so this part supplies the verb be
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen who wears the crown

explanation.surface: A girl wonders whether she might one day be crowned queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Read with the end of 7 down: that spice word, 'possibly with it', makes a fizzy drink. 'To wear the crown' is to BE ER, to be the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink can follow the spice of 7 down to name a soft drink, so it may go with it.

clue.text: Texan should remember to remove ends from sausage with love

indicators.note: the outer letters of the sausage word are dropped, keeping its middle

parts.note: salami is a kind of cured sausage
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A Texan is told to strip a sausage and add some affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The Texan battle cry is 'Remember the Alamo!', referring to the 1836 siege of the mission fort at San Antonio.
explanation.definitionFit: The rallying cry of Texan independence urged people to keep this besieged fort in their memory.

clue.text: This is asking for trouble … "Who I use to iron"

indicators.note: a setup asking for trouble is a mess about to happen, so the words Who I use are thrown into disorder

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A man risks a row by saying he uses his wife for ironing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This' points at the speaker the whole line describes; 'asking for trouble' rearranges WHO I USE into HOUSEWI, and FE (iron) completes it. The surface itself is asking for trouble, the setter's joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The quoted line is what a chauvinist might say of the woman who keeps house, the role the clue describes.

clue.text: Spend more scattering a bit of flower seed

indicators.note: scattering the letters of spend more spreads them into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener complains that sowing seed costs more money.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the nutritive tissue inside a flowering plant's seed, one part of the seed.

clue.text: Opposites preserving time for 8

indicators.note: preserving means the opposites hold the time word between them

parts.note: left and right are opposites, abbreviated L and R
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Contrary forces keep the clock for the drink at 8.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' means the solution at 8 down, a drink; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale bottom-fermented drink is a type of the brewed beverage at 8 down.

clue.text: Note writer, one will take risks

parts.note: G is a musical note
Eric Ambler was an English thriller writer

explanation.surface: A note from an author about taking chances.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who bets is by nature someone who takes risks for gain.

clue.text: 31 bringing torment turning up in the morning, sadly in the morning brought up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the torment word from bottom to top

parts.note: to rag is to tease or torment
AM stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

indicators.note: brought up reverses, in this down clue, the run made of the sad cry and the morning letters

parts.note: alas is a cry said sadly
again AM, the abbreviation for the morning hours

explanation.surface: Someone's morning brings torment, and sadness rises in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: '31' means the solution at 31 across, a spice. 'Turning up' turns RAG into GAR; 'brought up' turns ALAS plus AM into MASALA. 'Bringing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This Indian blend of ground spices is itself an example of a spice mix.

clue.text: I said pearl should be reset — by us?

indicators.note: a gem being reset is mounted anew, so the letters of I said pearl are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jeweller suggests a pearl needs a new setting and offers to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By us?' is the gem cutters speaking: they are the ones who would reset a pearl.
explanation.definitionFit: Gem cutters and polishers are the craftsmen who might reset a jewel, so the speakers are such workers.

clue.text: Leader of guides and peaceful girl turning a hundred in a class of their own

definitions.text: in a class of their own

indicators.note: leader of asks for the first letter of guides
turning reads the girl's name backwards

parts.note: Irene is a girl's name from the Greek for peace
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A Guide captain and a calm girl revolve around a hundred others.
explanation.definitionFit: Applying to a whole class or genus of things, rather than one particular brand or member.

clue.text: 31 to enter, if mispronounced?

indicators.note: if mispronounced says the phrase is spoken carelessly to make the answer's sound

parts.note: to enter a room is to come in

explanation.surface: Someone is invited inside, but the invitation is badly spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: '31' means the solution at 31 across, a spice.
explanation.definitionFit: These aromatic seeds are an example of a spice, used in curries and Mexican food.

clue.text: Some theorem appears to transform a function once more

definitions.text: to transform a function once more

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mathematical result seems to change a function again.
explanation.definitionFit: To map again is to apply a fresh mapping, which in maths means a new function transformation.

clue.text: Encourage — say "good"

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means in 'take, say, three'

explanation.surface: Urging someone on by calling them good.
explanation.definitionFit: To egg someone on is to urge or encourage them to act.

clue.text: In the beginning, God provided a minor form of illumination

indicators.note: in the beginning takes the opening letter of God

parts.note: minor and slight both mean small or trivial

explanation.surface: Echoing Genesis, God made a small light at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes Genesis, 'In the beginning God created...'; 'provided' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas lamps lit Victorian streets and homes, so this is a type of lighting.

clue.text: Go back to amateur operator writing system of old

indicators.note: go back tells us to read the word go backwards

parts.note: a ham is an amateur radio operator

explanation.surface: A radio amateur is told to return to an ancient script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An early medieval alphabet of strokes used in Ireland for inscriptions on stones.

clue.text: Rich, or if poor, frightful

indicators.note: poor here means badly done, so the letters of rich or if are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Whether wealthy or destitute, life is dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean causing horror or great fear.

clue.text: Round the bend a river ebbing, seeking stones on the way

indicators.note: an ebbing tide flows back, so the whole run is read backwards

parts.note: round the bend is slang for crazy, mad
the Cam is the river through Cambridge

explanation.surface: A river ebbs round a bend while someone looks for stones on the path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ebbing' turns MAD+A+CAM back to front as one run; 'seeking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Road surface of compacted broken stones, named after John McAdam, laid on the way.

clue.text: 31 not what it's supposed to be, they say

indicators.note: they say signals a word that sounds the same as the answer

parts.words: not what it's supposed to be
parts.note: this spice should be hot, so cold, chilly, is the opposite of what it is meant to be

explanation.surface: Something spoken of turns out unlike its reputation.
explanation.walkthrough: '31' means the solution at 31 across, a spice. The pepper should be hot, so it would be wrong for it to be cold.
explanation.definitionFit: This hot pepper, dried and ground, is an example of a fiery spice.

clue.text: See 13
31 of second insult incomplete

indicators.note: incomplete says the insult word loses its final letter

parts.note: an affront is an insult

explanation.surface: A second slight leaves something unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: '31' means the solution at 31 across, a spice; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Made from crocus stigmas, this costly yellow flavouring is an example of a spice.

clue.text: Mendicant service revolves around religion

indicators.note: around places the turned service letters on either side of the religion letters
revolves turns the service letters backwards

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
RI is religious instruction, the school subject

explanation.surface: A church service turns on matters of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: RI, Religious Instruction, is the old British school name for RE; 'revolves' turns RAF into FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicant orders live by begging, and such a brother is a member of one.

clue.text: Just for entertainment

definitions.meaning: just here means equitable, reasonable, impartial
a funfair with rides and stalls, an outing for entertainment

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is equitable and impartial; the other is a travelling funfair with rides and stalls.

clue.text: Yet what's said to reflect art is art!

parts.note: still and yet both mean nevertheless
the saying goes that art reflects life, so here life is what art mirrors

explanation.surface: Even so, a work that mirrors life is truly art.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the second 'art': a painting of fruit, flowers or objects is a genre of art.
explanation.definitionFit: A painting of inanimate objects such as fruit or flowers is a classic genre of art.

clue.text: Record of composer heard

indicators.note: heard signals that the composer's name is spoken to give the answer

parts.note: Franz Liszt was the Hungarian composer

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a record of a composer they listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An itemised record or register of names or things.

clue.text: Description of number, but not the first?

definitions.text: Description of number, but not the first?

indicators.note: but not the first drops the opening letter of the number

parts.note: seven is a number

explanation.surface: Is this a description of a number other than one?
explanation.walkthrough: Whole clue as definition and wordplay: the result describes a number like two, and the first number, one, is not.
explanation.definitionFit: Divisible by two describes a number, and the first number, one, is not such a number.

clue.text: Poor state of Alabama in hell hit badly

indicators.note: in puts the state letters inside the jumbled letters
badly means the letters of hell hit are jumbled

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: A southern US state suffers a hellish battering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' scrambles the two words to ILLHETH before the state's letters go in; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sick or unwell is a poor bodily state.

clue.text: Jelly topped with drug brings excitement

indicators.note: topped removes the first letter of the jelly word

parts.note: aspic is a savoury jelly
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone tops their jelly with a drug for a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: Spice in the sense of zest or added interest, as in the spice of life.
